Published online:
August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States (with geopolitical context: Iran / Strait of Hormuz)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps Friday's gold selloff and Warsh's Jackson Hole comments
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — upcoming ADP, NFP data; September rate hike probability; oil/inflation trajectory
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Gold is under pressure near a two-week low as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks sharply repriced September rate hike odds (36% → 64%). Rising oil prices driven by a US strike on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz are amplifying inflation concerns, strengthening both the USD and US yields — a dual headwind for gold. Markets are now focused on ADP and NFP prints for further rate guidance. Despite the daily pullback, gold remains on track for its best monthly performance since January (+9.7%).

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the rate hike repricing, USD strength, and yield dynamics are the central drivers of the entire narrative)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly yes — hawkish Fed pivot and rising rate hike bets are the dominant theme)
Probability of increase: 64% (as cited directly from CME FedWatch for September)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (only implicitly — holding is the prior baseline now being displaced)
Probability of holding: 36% (implied residual from CME FedWatch data)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are entirely absent from the article's framing)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (distinctly more hawkish — Warsh's Jackson Hole signal, the jump in hike probability, stronger USD, rising yields, and oil-driven inflation fears all reinforce a tightening bias with near-term catalyst risk from NFP)
